dehydrated_text:
Don't fight the Greeks head on. They will destroy your army. The entire Persian Navy is scattered; the war is over because Persians lost their naval mobility. Athenians will destroy what remains of the Persian navy.

Once you lose your navy, you can't resupply and lose the war. This is from Herodotus. Xerxes, realizing he's outmatched, decides to leave Greece. His general Monius sends an envoy to Athens, offering compensation for the destruction caused in exchange for peace.

Athenians reject this offer, stating their commitment to liberty and not fearing a greater Persian army. When Xerxes leaves, Mardonius is left in charge of the remaining forces. Spartans face off against Mardonis at Plataea and defeat him; Mardonius is killed.

One Spartan soldier suggests beheading Mardonius's corpse as revenge for Leonidas's death. Passenius rejects this, saying he admires their intentions but finds it inappropriate to insult a dead enemy.
